title: The Life That Gets Low
tagline: The life that gets low is the life God lifts.
seo_title: The Life That Gets Low: Hidden Service for Men | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Most men want to rise; few are willing to go low. A devotional on Luke 8, Matthew 25 and Philippians 2 about hidden service and who you're becoming.
verse_text: These women were helping to support them out of their own means.

scriptures.text: These women were helping to support them out of their own means.
Whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.
Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility, value others above yourselves.

items: Few are willing to lower themselves.

blocks.text: But in the Kingdom, the men who go low are the ones God lifts high.
Service is not weakness. It's evidence of transformation.
If your life only revolves around you, it's not freedom. It's limitation.
We love the idea of purpose. But we often miss how it actually shows up.
Not in stages. Not in spotlights. Not in recognition.
In service.
Luke 8 quietly reveals something powerful. While Jesus was doing the visible work, there were people behind the scenes making it possible: funding it, supporting it, sustaining it.
No spotlight. No applause. Just contribution.
And Jesus didn't overlook it. He recorded it. Why? Because in the Kingdom, what looks small to man is seen fully by God.
Most men think purpose looks like leading, building, being seen and being followed.
But Matthew 25 flips it: feeding someone, clothing someone, showing up for someone, caring for someone.
That's where Jesus says, "You did that for Me."
Let that land. The way you treat people is the way you treat Him. So service isn't just a good deed. It's a direct interaction with Christ.
Philippians 2 doesn't just give instruction. It reveals identity.
Jesus, who had every right to be served, chose to serve. He lowered Himself. He emptied Himself. He gave Himself.
Not once. Not occasionally. As a lifestyle.
And that's the invitation. Not random acts of service, but a restructured life.
You don't drift into service. You drift into self.
Service is intentional. It requires awareness, margin, humility and interruptibility.
And here's the tension most men miss:
You can follow Jesus publicly and still live for yourself privately.
But a man who is being transformed becomes someone who looks for ways to get low. Not to be noticed. Not to feel good. But because it's who he's becoming.

items: Where am I choosing convenience over contribution?
Who around me needs something I've been overlooking?
What would it look like to "get low" in my current season?
I do not live for myself.
I am being shaped into someone who serves.
I will lower myself so others can be lifted.
And I trust God to see what others don't.

blocks.text: Today, practice hidden service. Do something that benefits someone else, without announcing it and without expecting anything back.
Support someone. Step in quietly. Meet a need before it's spoken.
The goal isn't visibility. It's transformation.
The life that gets low is the life God lifts.
